intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without a reservation. Ideal for the first full morning after a late arrival day, as the market is walkable from many central hotels in Ginza or Shimbashi.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Pop Culture District Walk
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon in Akihabara, Tokyo's electric town, browsing multi-floor electronics shops, retro game arcades, and anime merchandise stores. Visit Yodobashi Camera and smaller indie shops for hands-on tech culture immersion. Easily accessible by JR Yamanote Line, making it convenient from most central Tokyo hotels.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple at Senso-ji, strolling through Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks. Explore the surrounding Asakusa district for rickshaw rides and a glimpse into old Edo culture. Best experienced in the morning before crowds peak, and very close to budget-friendly hotels in the Asakusa area.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the world-renowned teamLab Borderless, a cutting-edge digital art museum blending technology and interactive installations. A perfect fusion of Tokyo's tech culture and artistic expression. Book tickets in advance online. The new Azabudai Hills location is centrally located and easily reachable from Roppongi or Minato area hotels.

experiences.name: Shinjuku Izakaya Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Spend an evening in Shinjuku's Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) and surrounding izakayas, enjoying yakitori, ramen, and local sake in a lively, authentic atmosphere. This area is ideal for late-night dining, perfect for travelers arriving late on Day 1 who want to ease into Tokyo's food scene without a long commute. Many hotels in Shinjuku place you steps away.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Narita Express (N'EX) or Limousine Bus to Chiyoda City. Budget tip: use IC card (Suica or Pasmo) purchased at the airport for cheaper train fares.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay, freshen up, then take a relaxed walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (free entry) to get your bearings and enjoy the spring cherry blossom remnants in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Akihabara Electric Town (10–15 min walk/train from Chiyoda) — window shop tech stores, anime shops, and game centers. Great introduction to Tokyo's tech culture with no entry costs.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab an onigiri (rice ball) from a convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) at the airport for ¥120–¥180.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a bento box from a convenience store near the hotel for ¥450–¥600.
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local Akihabara ramen shop such as a chain like Ichiran or a local spot — budget ¥800–¥1,200 per bowl.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the airport (¥500 deposit + load funds). Keep jet lag in mind — don't over-schedule the first evening. April in Tokyo averages 14–18°C, bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market (free to walk around) for a morning food experience. Try fresh tamagoyaki (egg omelette) skewers, grilled scallops, and fresh tuna sushi from market stalls for ¥200–¥500 per item.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond. Then stroll through Ginza window shopping (free) to observe Tokyo's upscale culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome/Shimbashi area for dinner. Explore the Shimbashi salaryman izakaya alleys for authentic, cheap Japanese pub food.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market street food — fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and green tea for ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Teishoku (set meal) at a local diner near Ginza for ¥800–¥1,200 — rice, miso soup, grilled fish included.
meals.dinner: Izakaya in Shimbashi — order yakitori skewers, edamame, and a draft beer for ¥1,500–¥2,500 total.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited before 11:00 for the freshest food and smaller crowds. Hamarikyu is a short walk from Tsukiji.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ueno Park (free entry) — visit Ueno Zoo (¥600), stroll past Shinobazu Pond, and admire the Toshogu Shrine. Great for culture and nature combined.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (¥1,000) — Japan's largest museum covering Japanese art, samurai armor, pottery, and cultural artifacts. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Ameyoko Market street in Ueno — a lively open-air market with cheap street food, fresh produce, and bargain goods. Great evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki sandwich, and canned coffee for ¥350–¥500.
meals.lunch: Ramen or udon at a restaurant near Ueno station for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Street food at Ameyoko Market — yakitori, takoyaki (octopus balls), and fresh fruit for ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is one of Tokyo's best cherry blossom spots — even in mid-April you may catch late-blooming varieties. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Asakusa — visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry), Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early (before 9:00) to avoid crowds. Walk Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (¥600) — fascinating exhibits on the history of Tokyo from Edo period to modern times, highly relevant to cultural interests.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Asakusa for the evening atmosphere around Senso-ji when it's lit up. Walk along the Sumida River for skyline views including Tokyo Skytree (exterior view is free).

meals.breakfast: Ningyo-yaki (small cakes) and matcha from a stall on Nakamise Street for ¥300–¥500.
meals.lunch: Tempura tendon (tempura rice bowl) at a local Asakusa restaurant for ¥900–¥1,300.
meals.dinner: Monja-yaki or okonomiyaki (savory pancakes) at a budget restaurant near Asakusa for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free but the surrounding area has many paid attractions. Stick to free temple grounds and Nakamise Street to stay on budget. Ryogoku is one stop from Asakusa by train.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Akihabara in depth — visit multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera (free to browse), retro game shops, and the famous Akihabara Radio Kaikan building packed with tech and hobby shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Science Museum (Kagaku Gijutsukan) near Kitanomaru Park in Chiyoda (¥600) — hands-on science and technology exhibits reflecting Japan's tech culture. Then walk through Kitanomaru Park (free).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the rooftop observation deck of Kitte Marunouchi building (free) near Tokyo Station for panoramic views of the station and city skyline at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Yoshinoya or Matsuya gyudon (beef rice bowl) chain near hotel for ¥400–¥500 — classic cheap Japanese breakfast.
meals.lunch: Curry rice at a CoCo Ichibanya or local curry shop in Akihabara for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at a chain like Sushiro or Hamazushi near Tokyo Station — ¥100–¥150 per plate, budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is the heart of Tokyo's tech and otaku culture — perfect for your interests. Many shops open around 10:00–11:00. The Science Museum is closed on Fridays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500) — one of Japan's finest gardens combining Japanese, French, and English landscape styles. Late cherry blossoms and spring flowers may still be blooming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's Kabukicho entertainment district and the free observation deck at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free, open until 22:30 most nights) for stunning panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in Shinjuku — tiny alley packed with tiny yakitori and ramen stalls. Atmospheric and budget-friendly evening dining.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or bakery near the hotel for ¥300–¥500.
meals.lunch: Katsu curry or tonkatsu set meal at a Shinjuku diner for ¥850–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Yakitori skewers and beer at Omoide Yokocho — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 for a satisfying meal with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free — one of the best views in Tokyo at no cost. Go at sunset for the best experience. Shinjuku is about 30 min by train from Chiyoda.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku — visit Meiji Shrine (free entry into grounds, ¥1,000 for inner garden) surrounded by forested parkland. A peaceful and culturally rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for youth fashion culture and cheap street food (crepes, cotton candy, etc.). Then stroll Omotesando Avenue for architecture and window shopping (free).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya — experience the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at night. Visit Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000) for a spectacular rooftop view, or use the free Shibuya Hikarie sky lobby for a budget alternative.

meals.breakfast: Crepe from a Takeshita Street stall (¥500–¥700) or convenience store near hotel.
meals.lunch: Ramen at Ichiran Harajuku (solo dining ramen booths) for ¥980–¥1,200 — a unique cultural experience.
meals.dinner: Izakaya near Shibuya station — set dinner menus available for ¥1,500–¥2,500 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is a must-see for cultural immersion. If budget is tight, skip Shibuya Sky (¥2,000) and use the free Mag's Park rooftop at Shibuya 109 or Starbucks Reserve Roastery Shibuya (no entry fee, just buy a coffee).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Walk Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse old temples and cemeteries. Free to explore and deeply cultural.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nezu Shrine (free entry) — famous for its hundreds of torii gates and azalea gardens which bloom in mid-to-late April. Then explore the Nezu/Yanesen area cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Akihabara for evening gaming — visit a multi-floor arcade (game center) like Taito Station or Sega for ¥100–¥200 per game. Great tech culture experience.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel for coffee and toast set — ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Menchi-katsu (fried meat cutlet) or croquette from a Yanaka Ginza deli stall for ¥150–¥200 each — a famous local snack.
meals.dinner: Soba noodles at a traditional soba restaurant in Yanaka or Ueno area for ¥700–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of Tokyo's most authentic neighborhoods — largely untouched by modern development. Nezu Shrine's azalea festival (Tsutsuji Matsuri) runs late April, so timing is perfect. Entry to the azalea garden may cost ¥200.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — take the Yurikamome monorail (scenic ride, ¥330 one way) to this futuristic artificial island. Visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum (¥3,200) — a world-famous immersive tech-art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's free attractions: Palette Town, the giant Gundam statue outside DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, and the beachside park with views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Odaiba Aqua City mall (free to browse) and watch the Rainbow Bridge light up at night before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel before departing — ¥300–¥500.
meals.lunch: Food court at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza — ramen, curry, or donburi for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Odaiba Aqua City food floor — various Japanese options including sushi, ramen, and tempura for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless is pricier (¥3,200) but considered a bucket-list experience combining tech and art. Book tickets online in advance to avoid sellouts. If budget is tight, skip teamLab and spend more time at free Odaiba attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koenji neighborhood — known for vintage clothing, indie music culture, and local artisan shops. Walk the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) for a glimpse of authentic local Tokyo life. Free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nakano Broadway complex (free entry) — a legendary multi-floor shopping center famous for vintage manga, anime collectibles, and retro tech. A hidden gem of Tokyo's otaku and tech culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood with live music venues, vintage shops, and cozy cafes. Great evening atmosphere for culture lovers.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery in Koenji for fresh-baked melon pan and coffee — ¥350–¥500.
meals.lunch: Curry at a local Koenji restaurant — the area is known for excellent, affordable curry spots for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Small izakaya or ramen shop in Shimokitazawa — ¥1,000–¥1,500. Many have standing bars (tachinomi) for cheaper drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Koenji and Shimokitazawa are favorite neighborhoods of Tokyo locals rather than tourists — great for authentic cultural immersion. Both are about 20–30 min from Chiyoda by train on the Chuo line.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi (¥1,800 — includes Tokyo City View observation deck) — contemporary art with panoramic city views from the 53rd floor of Mori Tower. Opens at 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi Hills and the free outdoor Mori Garden (traditional Japanese garden, free). Walk to Azabu-Juban neighborhood — a charming, upscale-but-walkable local shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Zojoji Temple (free) near Tokyo Tower — beautiful Buddhist temple with Tokyo Tower as a dramatic backdrop, especially stunning when lit up at night. Great photo opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or Pronto cafe chain near hotel for ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Lunch set at a local Roppongi restaurant — many offer affordable lunch specials (¥900–¥1,300) that are cheaper than dinner menus.
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) at a local Azabu or Roppongi restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View combo ticket (¥1,800) is excellent value. Tokyo Tower exterior view from Zojoji Temple is completely free and arguably more photogenic than paying to go up the tower.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous book town in Chiyoda City (walkable from hotel). Dozens of secondhand bookshops, antique map dealers, and academic publishers line the streets. Free to browse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) in Kitanomaru Park, Chiyoda (¥500) — Japan's first national art museum with impressive Japanese modern and contemporary art collections.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening stroll around the Imperial Palace moat (free, beautifully lit at night) and Marunouchi district. Visit the Marunouchi Brick Square and Tokyo Station's historic red-brick facade for photos.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a local diner in Chiyoda — rice, miso soup, grilled fish set for ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Soba noodles at a Jimbocho soba restaurant — the area has excellent affordable options for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Yakiniku (grilled meat) at a budget yakiniku restaurant in Marunouchi or Akihabara for ¥1,500–¥2,500 — a celebratory penultimate night dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Jimbocho is right in your hotel's neighborhood — perfect for a relaxed day close to home. MOMAT is closed on Mondays. The Imperial Palace moat walk takes about 45–60 minutes at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit a favorite neighborhood or market. Recommended: early morning visit to Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell fresh sushi breakfast. Alternatively, take a final peaceful walk through the Imperial Palace East Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Don Quijote (discount variety store, open 24 hours) in Akihabara or Shinjuku — best prices on snacks, cosmetics, and small gifts. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation — check out of hotel, head to airport. Take Narita Express or Airport Limousine from Tokyo Station (5–10 min walk from Chiyoda hotel). Arrive airport 2–3 hours before flight.

meals.breakfast: Farewell sushi breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — splurge slightly for ¥1,000–¥1,500 on fresh tuna and uni sushi as a final treat.
meals.lunch: Ekiben (station bento box) purchased at Tokyo Station for the journey — ¥800–¥1,200. Tokyo Station has Japan's best ekiben selection.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Don Quijote (Donki) is the best place for budget souvenirs and snacks to bring home. Budget ¥2,000–¥5,000 for final souvenir shopping. Keep transit costs in mind for airport transfer — Narita Express from Tokyo Station costs ¥3,070, or take a cheaper highway bus for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Chiyoda City. Check in to the Chiyoda City Boutique Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation walk around the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen) — free entry, beautifully maintained, and just minutes from most Chiyoda hotels. Enjoy the cherry blossom aftermath or spring greenery. Stroll along the moat toward Nijubashi Bridge for iconic views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Yurakucho area (5–10 min walk) for your first Tokyo dinner. Explore the atmospheric alleyways under the train tracks filled with yakitori stalls and izakayas. Perfect low-key introduction to Tokyo nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a bento box at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up an onigiri, sandwich, or hot meal from a convenience store or airport food court en route to the hotel (¥500–¥900).
meals.dinner: Yurakucho Yakitori Alley — grilled skewers, cold beer, and salaryman atmosphere. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport or hotel area convenience store for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. Download Google Maps offline and the Tokyo Metro app.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tsukiji Outer Market (30 min by train or taxi from Chiyoda) — browse fresh seafood stalls, tamagoyaki shops, and specialty food vendors. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM for the best experience before crowds peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short train ride to Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional garden with a teahouse on the water, contrasting beautifully with the surrounding skyscrapers. Afterward, take a water bus up the Sumida River toward Asakusa (¥1,000, scenic ride).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's Nakamise Shopping Street leading to Senso-ji Temple. The temple is illuminated at night and far less crowded. Browse traditional crafts, ningyo-yaki cakes, and paper fans as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh tuna sashimi don or grilled scallops from market stalls. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse — matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets) for a cultural lunch break (¥1,000). Supplement with a nearby ramen shop in Tsukishima.
meals.dinner: Asakusa — try Kaminarimon area restaurants for tempura (Daikokuya Tempura is iconic) or eel (unaju). Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited early. The inner wholesale market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains a food lover's paradise. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking today.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara Electric Town — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district, just one stop from central Chiyoda. Explore multi-story electronics stores like Yodobashi Akihabara, retro game shops, and gadget markets. Perfect for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara — visit the Radio Kaikan building (8 floors of hobby, anime, and tech goods), explore retro game arcades (Super Potato is a must), and check out maid cafés for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a short train to Ueno for dinner, then visit Ueno Park for an evening stroll. Check out Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) market street — a bustling outdoor market with street food, clothing, and local goods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a Japanese morning set (tamago gohan, miso soup, grilled fish) at a local kissaten (traditional coffee shop). Budget ¥700–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Akihabara — grab a quick curry rice or ramen at a local restaurant. Try Curry House CoCo Ichibanya for customizable Japanese curry. Budget ¥900–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market area in Ueno — fresh seafood bowls, takoyaki, yakitori skewers, and more from street stalls. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best experienced on a weekday morning when it's less crowded. Many shops open around 10–11 AM. Bring cash — some smaller shops don't accept cards. Ameyoko is liveliest in the early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours from Shinjuku/Ueno by Tobu Nikko Line or Shinkansen). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate, gold-gilded mausoleums set among ancient cedar forests. Arrive early to beat weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Rinnoji Temple and Futarasan Shrine within the Nikko shrine complex. Walk the cedar-lined avenue (Sugi Namiki) and visit Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. Optional: hike toward Kegon Falls (20 min bus ride).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relax in the hotel or take a quiet walk around the Imperial Palace outer gardens lit by lampposts.

meals.breakfast: Grab an ekiben (station bento box) at Ueno or Asakusa station before boarding — a classic Japanese travel tradition. Budget ¥900–¥1,400.
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine is the local specialty. Try a yuba soba set at a restaurant near Tosho-gu. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Back in Chiyoda — visit Kanda area for a bowl of Kanda Yabu Soba (one of Tokyo's most historic soba restaurants, est. 1880). Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko Pass for unlimited travel on the Tobu Line and discounts at attractions (approx. ¥4,000 round trip from Asakusa). Nikko can be cold even in April — bring a light jacket. Book soba dinner early as Yabu Soba closes when they run out.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku and Meiji Jingu Shrine — start with the serene forested shrine, a spiritual oasis in the heart of the city. The torii gate entrance and gravel path through ancient trees is deeply atmospheric on a Sunday morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street for Harajuku's famous youth fashion and quirky street food (crepes, cotton candy, rainbow toast). Then shift to the adjacent Omotesando avenue for upscale boutiques, concept stores, and architectural gems like Prada and Louis Vuitton buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya — experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing at dusk. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000) for panoramic sunset views over the city. Explore Shibuya's vibrant restaurant and bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku — bills Japan in Omotesando for famous ricotta pancakes (splurge breakfast, ¥2,000–¥3,000) or a simpler bakery option at Viron Boulangerie.
meals.lunch: Omotesando Hills food basement (B2F) — curated Japanese food stalls and bento options. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Shibuya — try Ichiran Ramen (solo ramen booths, a unique cultural experience) or explore the restaurant floors of Shibuya Hikarie. Budget ¥1,500–¥3,000.

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic at dusk or night. The Shibuya Sky deck is best booked online in advance. Sunday in Harajuku means cosplay performers near the park entrance — a great photo opportunity.

day_by_day.morning: Odaiba — futuristic waterfront island accessible by the driverless Yurikamome monorail (scenic ride itself). Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book tickets well in advance) — immersive digital art installations that sit at the intersection of tech and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Odaiba's DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (life-size Gundam statue outside), the retro-futuristic Palette Town area, and the Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) — Japan's premier science museum with robots, space tech, and AI exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset view of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline from Odaiba's waterfront promenade. Return to central Tokyo via the Yurikamome or water bus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby kissaten in Chiyoda before departing for Odaiba.
meals.lunch: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza food court — diverse options including ramen, burgers, and Japanese sets. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Return to Ginza area near Chiyoda — explore Ginza Six basement food hall (B2F) for gourmet bento, sushi, and wagashi. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets MUST be booked online in advance — they frequently sell out weeks ahead. Miraikan is excellent for tech enthusiasts and has English displays throughout. The Yurikamome monorail is worth the ride for views alone.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku — start at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free observation deck, opens 9:30 AM) for panoramic city views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding Nishi-Shinjuku skyscraper district, a showcase of Japanese corporate architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to East Shinjuku — explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (one of Japan's finest parks, ¥500 entry). Afterward, wander through Kabukicho entertainment district and the compact, atmospheric Golden Gai bar alley.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night — the neon-lit Kabukicho area, Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) with tiny smoky yakitori stalls, and the energy of one of the world's busiest train stations.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku — Keio Department Store basement (B1) for fresh pastries and Japanese morning items. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style — buy a bento from a nearby convenience store or Takashimaya Times Square basement and eat in the garden. Budget ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny grilled skewer shops under the train tracks. Atmospheric, affordable, and authentically local. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 6 people) and some have cover charges of ¥500–¥1,000. They are welcoming to tourists. Shinjuku Gyoen closes Mondays — confirmed open Tuesday. The observation deck offers the best Mt. Fuji views on clear winter/spring mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station). Start at the Great Buddha of Kotoku-in (Kamakura Daibutsu) — a 13-meter bronze statue set against forested hills. Explore Hase-dera Temple with its sea views and cave shrines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forest to Zeniarai Benten Shrine (a cave shrine where you wash money for good fortune). Descend into Kamakura town and explore Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Optional stop at Yokohama's Chinatown (en route) for dinner before heading back to Chiyoda.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab a convenience store breakfast at Tokyo Station before boarding. Budget ¥500–¥900.
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl is the local specialty. Try a shirasu don at a restaurant near Hase Station. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Yokohama Chinatown (optional detour) — dim sum, Peking duck, and Chinese-Japanese fusion dishes. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500. Or return to Chiyoda for a simple ramen dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Use a JR Pass (if purchased) or buy a single ticket from Tokyo Station. The Kamakura–Enoshima Pass (¥700) covers local Enoden tram rides. The hiking trail takes 60–90 minutes and requires sturdy shoes. Avoid rainy days for this excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Yanaka District — Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhood. Wander through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, explore the atmospheric cemetery (where many famous Japanese figures are buried), and browse independent craft shops and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Nezu and Yanesen area. Visit Nezu Shrine — a smaller, less-visited alternative to Fushimi Inari with rows of torii gates and seasonal flowers. Walk to the nearby Scai the Bathhouse — a contemporary art gallery in a converted 200-year-old bathhouse.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (short train ride) for a second, more focused visit — specifically for retro gaming, anime culture, or any tech items you missed. End the evening with dinner in the Kanda area.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — fresh melon pan, croquettes, and handmade tofu from local vendors. Budget ¥500–¥900.
meals.lunch: Yanaka area — a traditional shokudo (set-meal diner) serving teishoku (set lunch with rice, miso, fish/meat). Budget ¥900–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Kanda — explore the many ramen shops and izakayas. Try Kanda Matsuya for soba or a local tonkatsu restaurant. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of the few areas that survived WWII bombing and the 1923 earthquake, preserving Edo-period urban character. Many shops are closed on Wednesdays — confirmed open Thursday. Bring cash as many small shops are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Roppongi — visit the Mori Art Museum (52nd floor of Mori Tower, ¥2,000) for contemporary Japanese and international art with stunning city views from the adjacent observation deck. Roppongi is Tokyo's art district with world-class galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Art Center Tokyo (free entry to building, exhibition fees vary) — Japan's largest exhibition space with rotating major shows. Nearby 21_21 Design Sight (by Tadao Ando) offers design-focused exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Roppongi Hills or Tokyo Midtown for evening dining and drinks. These upscale complexes have excellent mid-range dining options and are beautifully lit at night. Explore the outdoor art installations in Midtown Garden.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near Chiyoda before heading to Roppongi. Budget ¥700–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: National Art Center Tokyo — the museum's brasserie has a famous giant inverted cone display and serves French-Japanese lunch sets. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Tokyo Midtown — Gonpachi Nishi-Azabu (the 'Kill Bill restaurant') or explore the Midtown dining floors for Japanese cuisine. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on Fridays — ideal for a late start. The observation deck (Tokyo City View) is included with the museum ticket. Roppongi has a vibrant nightlife scene if you want to extend your evening.

day_by_day.morning: Toyosu Market — the world's largest wholesale fish market (replaced Tsukiji's inner market). Book the observation area tour in advance to watch the famous tuna auction (lottery system, very limited). Explore the market buildings and seafood restaurants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural district, a short distance from Chiyoda. Visit the Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors, a Japanese cultural institution), the Sony Park interactive experience, and browse the Ginza Six complex.
day_by_day.evening: Ginza at night is elegant and walkable. Visit the Okuno Building — a 1932 art deco building housing dozens of tiny artist studios and galleries open to visitors. End with a stroll along Chuo-dori (car-free on weekends).

meals.breakfast: Toyosu Market — fresh sushi breakfast at one of the market's sushi restaurants. A classic Tokyo experience. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500.
meals.lunch: Ginza — basement food halls of Mitsukoshi or Matsuya department stores offer premium bento, sashimi, and sweets. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Ginza area — try Kyubey (renowned sushi, slightly splurge) or a mid-range tempura restaurant. Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 for a special dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Tuna auctions at Toyosu require advance lottery registration on the Toyosu Market website — apply well before the trip. The observation area (no auction) is easier to access. Ginza's Chuo-dori becomes a pedestrian zone on weekend afternoons — great for strolling.

day_by_day.morning: Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood known for vintage clothing, indie music venues, and a creative, youthful atmosphere. Browse the dozens of thrift and vintage stores, independent bookshops, and record stores. A window into Tokyo's alternative culture scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nakameguro — walk along the Meguro River (lined with cherry trees, beautiful even after bloom season with fresh green leaves). Explore the trendy boutiques, cafés, and design shops along the riverbank. Visit the Daikanyama T-Site bookstore complex — an architectural and cultural landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Ebisu and Daikanyama for a relaxed final full-evening dinner. These upscale but approachable neighborhoods have excellent restaurants, wine bars, and craft beer spots.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa — a local kissaten (old-school coffee shop) for morning coffee and toast set. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Nakameguro — one of the many river-side cafés or a Japanese curry lunch at a local spot. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Ebisu — Log Road Daikanyama area or Ebisu Garden Place for a relaxed dinner. Try Tableaux (European-Japanese fusion) or a local izakaya. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best explored slowly and spontaneously — don't over-plan. Many vintage stores open around 11–12 AM. Daikanyama T-Site is as much a lifestyle concept as a bookstore — the architecture and curation are worth experiencing even without buying.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit a favorite neighborhood or spot you want to see one more time. Alternatively, visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku (if not already visited) for a comprehensive look at Tokyo's history from the Edo period to modern day. Or spend a peaceful final morning at the Imperial Palace East Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir gathering — return to Akihabara for tech goods, Ginza for premium Japanese crafts, or Asakusa for traditional souvenirs. Don't forget: Japanese Kit-Kat flavors, wagashi sweets, and stationery from Itoya make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Pack, check out, and transfer to the airport. Allow 2–2.5 hours before departure. Grab a final convenience store onigiri or airport ramen for a true Tokyo farewell.

meals.breakfast: A final Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten near the hotel — savor tamago gohan (egg on rice), miso soup, and pickles one last time. Budget ¥700–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Depachika (department store basement) near your last shopping stop — assemble a final bento from premium stalls. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Airport — Narita or Haneda have excellent ramen and sushi restaurants airside. Treat yourself to a proper final Japanese meal before departure. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo (Narita Express from Tokyo Station, ¥3,070). Haneda is closer at 30–40 minutes. Confirm your departure airport. Remember to claim consumption tax refunds at the airport tax refund counter for eligible purchases made in Japan.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This is a must for food lovers wanting authentic Tokyo flavors without a reservation. Ideal for the first full morning after a late arrival day, as the market is walkable from many central hotels in Ginza or Shimbashi.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo — Flight LH lands at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration at Narita or Haneda, collect luggage, and arrange private airport transfer to Chiyoda City Boutique Stay. Settle into your luxury accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely orientation stroll through the Imperial Palace East Gardens (Higashi Gyoen), just minutes from Chiyoda. Enjoy the serene moats, stone walls, and early spring greenery. Stop at the Ninomaru Garden for a tranquil introduction to Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Tokyo's dining scene with dinner at a refined kaiseki restaurant in the Marunouchi district, such as Kitcho or a comparable multi-course kaiseki establishment. Enjoy the artful presentation of seasonal Japanese cuisine paired with premium sake or whisky.

meals.breakfast: Meal served on the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or bento box at the airport arrival hall or in-transit
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at a Michelin-recognized restaurant in Marunouchi — expect 12–15 courses of seasonal Japanese cuisine (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may be a factor — keep Day 1 light. Request a late check-in confirmation from the hotel in advance. The Imperial Palace Gardens close at 17:00 so time your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Join a premium guided food tour of the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh nigiri sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), grilled scallops, uni (sea urchin), and other delicacies from legendary stalls. Learn the history of Tokyo's greatest culinary institution from a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginza, Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district. Browse flagship stores of Japanese luxury brands such as Mikimoto, Issey Miyake, and Comme des Garçons. Visit the architecturally stunning Itoya stationery boutique and the Dover Street Market Ginza for cutting-edge fashion and design.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza location) or a comparable world-class sushi omakase counter. Watch master sushi chefs craft each piece tableside in an intimate 10-seat setting.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary hotel breakfast or light coffee and pastry at the hotel lounge
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market food tour — multiple tastings including fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks (included in tour)
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi dinner in Ginza — premium nigiri and seasonal seafood courses (¥40,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tsukiji food tour and omakase dinner well in advance — top omakase counters in Tokyo require reservations months ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market tour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku for a deep dive into the city's 400-year history — from Edo-period samurai culture to the post-war tech boom. Explore immersive full-scale reconstructions of old Edo streetscapes, kabuki theaters, and traditional merchant quarters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Sumida River to Asakusa and explore Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk the Nakamise-dori shopping arcade for premium traditional crafts, lacquerware, and sweets. Visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop for panoramic views of the Skytree.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634m) at dsunset for breathtaking panoramic views of the city. Dine at one of the tower's premium restaurants or descend to Asakusa for a traditional teppanyaki dinner at a high-end local establishment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — traditional Japanese set or Western buffet
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined tempura restaurant near Asakusa, such as Daikokuya Tempura (est. 1887) — crispy Edo-style tempura over rice (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki dinner in Asakusa or Skytree dining — premium Wagyu beef, seasonal vegetables, and fresh seafood prepared tableside (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is open 24 hours but most inner buildings close by 17:00. Book Tokyo Skytree tickets online in advance to skip queues. April evenings can be cool — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Akihabara Electric Town — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Visit multi-floor electronics megastores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera, explore retro video game shops, and browse the latest robotics, gadgets, and anime technology. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building for rare electronics and collector items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba island. Interact with ASIMO robots, explore AI and space technology exhibits, and experience cutting-edge VR and digital installations. Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum on Odaiba for an immersive, boundary-less digital art experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Odaiba with panoramic views of Tokyo Bay and the Rainbow Bridge. Opt for a French-Japanese fusion restaurant or a high-end seafood dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Akihabara — lunch at a high-end ramen specialist such as Fuunji or a premium katsu curry restaurant (¥2,000–¥4,000)
meals.dinner: Premium French-Japanese fusion or seafood restaurant in Odaiba with Rainbow Bridge views (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless requires advance online booking — tickets sell out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for extensive walking in Akihabara and Odaiba. The Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi to Odaiba offers scenic bay views.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — depart early by private car or the Tobu Nikko Limited Express from Asakusa Station (approx. 2 hours). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex, the ornate mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu. Marvel at the Yomeimon Gate (Gate of Sunlight), adorned with over 500 intricate carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's Rinno-ji Temple and the serene Shinkyo Sacred Bridge. Walk through the cedar-lined avenues of the shrine complex and visit the Taiyuin Mausoleum. Enjoy the surrounding Nikko National Park mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by private transfer or express train. Arrive back at the hotel by early evening. Dinner at a refined Japanese restaurant in Chiyoda or Marunouchi.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional ryotei (formal Japanese restaurant) in Nikko — regional cuisine including yuba (tofu skin) dishes, a Nikko specialty (¥5,000–¥10,000)
meals.dinner: Refined Japanese cuisine at a Chiyoda or Marunouchi restaurant upon return — perhaps a premium yakitori or robatayaki counter (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is approximately 150km from Tokyo. A private car is recommended for maximum comfort and flexibility. Entrance fees for Tosho-gu and surrounding temples are separate — budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person. Book Nikko lunch reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing over 110,000 artifacts including samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculptures, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Arrange a private guided tour for a curated, in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Ueno Park — one of Tokyo's most beloved green spaces, especially beautiful in cherry blossom season (late April). Visit Ueno Zoo or the Shitamachi Museum for a glimpse into old Tokyo working-class culture. Explore the Ameyoko market street for lively street food and local color.
day_by_day.evening: Experience an authentic Japanese cultural performance — book tickets to a Kabuki theater performance at the Kabuki-za Theater in Ginza (evening show typically starts at 16:30 or 18:00). Dinner at a premium restaurant nearby after the performance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium bento box lunch at the Tokyo National Museum restaurant or a refined soba restaurant in Ueno (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Post-Kabuki dinner at a high-end Ginza restaurant — French-Japanese cuisine or premium shabu-shabu (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Kabuki-za Theater tickets well in advance — single-act tickets (hitomaku-mi) are available for shorter visits if a full program is not preferred. Private museum guide can be arranged through the Tokyo National Museum website.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku and Omotesando — Tokyo's fashion and design hub. Begin with a quiet morning walk along the iconic Takeshita Street before the crowds arrive. Visit the Ota Memorial Museum of Art for an exquisite collection of ukiyo-e woodblock prints in a beautifully curated space.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's 'Champs-Élysées' — browsing flagship stores by Prada, Louis Vuitton, and Hermès, all housed in architecturally significant buildings designed by world-renowned architects. Visit the Nezu Museum for its stunning Japanese and Asian art collection and tranquil bamboo garden.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Omotesando or Aoyama at a celebrated chef's table restaurant. Consider L'Effervescence or a comparable innovative Japanese-French cuisine establishment with a seasonal tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium café or bistro on Omotesando — avocado toast with wagyu, or a refined Japanese lunch set (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Chef's table tasting menu dinner at L'Effervescence or equivalent — innovative Japanese-French cuisine with wine pairing (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Nezu Museum garden is particularly beautiful in spring. Book dinner reservations at L'Effervescence 2–3 months in advance. Omotesando flagship stores are generally open from 11:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private tea ceremony and Zen meditation experience — arrange an exclusive private session at a traditional tea house in the Yanaka or Shinjuku Gyoen area. Learn the philosophy and precise choreography of the Japanese tea ceremony (chado) from a certified tea master.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku — visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for free panoramic city views. Wander through the tranquil Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks. Explore the Takashimaya Times Square luxury department store for premium Japanese goods and food hall.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's legendary nightlife — begin with cocktails at a premium bar in the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (famous from the film Lost in Translation), then explore the atmospheric Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) alleyway for yakitori skewers and local whisky.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at the Shinjuku Takashimaya food hall or a refined Shinjuku kaiseki restaurant (¥5,000–¥10,000)
meals.dinner: New York Bar at Park Hyatt Tokyo for cocktails and light bites, followed by yakitori at Omoide Yokocho — a unique mix of luxury and local authenticity (¥15,000–¥25,000 combined)

day_by_day.notes: The private tea ceremony should be booked at least 2 weeks in advance through a cultural experience concierge. New York Bar has a cover charge on evenings with live jazz — check the schedule. Shinjuku Gyoen has a small entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art institutions, with rotating exhibitions featuring leading Japanese and international artists. The museum occupies the 53rd floor with stunning city views. Combine with a visit to the Tokyo City View observation deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (Japan's largest exhibition space) and the Suntory Museum of Art for traditional Japanese decorative arts. Walk through the Roppongi Hills complex and the Midtown Tokyo luxury retail and dining precinct.
day_by_day.evening: Private sake tasting and pairing dinner — arrange an exclusive sake sommelier experience at a premium nihonshu (sake) bar in Roppongi or Azabu, learning about regional breweries, rice varieties, and fermentation styles. Pair with seasonal Japanese small plates.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Roppongi Hills — contemporary Japanese cuisine with city views (¥5,000–¥10,000)
meals.dinner: Private sake pairing dinner at a premium nihonshu bar in Roppongi or Azabu-Juban — curated sake flights with seasonal Japanese small plates (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 on most days) — consider a morning visit to avoid crowds. The National Art Center is closed on Tuesdays. Book the sake tasting experience through a luxury concierge service.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved historic neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Walk through the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery lined with ancient cherry trees, browse the Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, and visit the Yanaka area's small temples and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the 21_21 Design Sight museum in Minami-Aoyama, founded by Issey Miyake and architect Tadao Ando — a world-class design museum with innovative exhibitions exploring everyday design. Explore the surrounding Aoyama cemetery and the boutique galleries of the Minami-Aoyama art district.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium tasting menu restaurant in Minami-Aoyama or Shibuya. Consider Quintessence or a comparable innovative Japanese-European cuisine establishment. Afterwards, explore the Shibuya Scramble Crossing at night — one of the world's most iconic urban spectacles.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a Yanaka neighborhood restaurant — handmade soba noodles or Japanese home-style cooking (¥2,000–¥4,000)
meals.dinner: Premium tasting menu restaurant in Aoyama or Shibuya — innovative multi-course Japanese-European cuisine (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. 21_21 Design Sight is closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. The Shibuya Scramble is most spectacular after dark — visit around 20:00–21:00 for maximum atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Private sushi-making masterclass — arrange an exclusive hands-on sushi workshop with a professional itamae (sushi chef) at a premium cooking studio in central Tokyo. Learn to prepare shari (vinegared rice), slice sashimi, and craft nigiri and maki under expert guidance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kagurazaka neighborhood — Tokyo's historic French quarter with deep Japanese roots. Walk the cobblestone Kagurazaka slope, explore hidden geisha alleyways (kakuriyo), browse artisan shops, and visit the Akagi Shrine — a striking modern Shinto shrine designed by architect Kengo Kuma.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Noh theater or Bunraku puppet theater performance arranged through a cultural concierge. Alternatively, experience a premium geisha ozashiki dinner party in Kagurazaka — an exclusive evening of traditional entertainment, games, and multi-course kaiseki cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Post-sushi class lunch — enjoy the sushi you prepared in class, supplemented by premium additions from the chef (included in workshop)
meals.dinner: Geisha ozashiki dinner in Kagurazaka — traditional multi-course kaiseki with geisha entertainment (¥50,000–¥100,000 per person, requires introduction/booking through concierge)

day_by_day.notes: An ozashiki dinner with geisha entertainment is one of the most exclusive experiences in Japan — book through a luxury hotel concierge or specialist cultural agency at least 4–6 weeks in advance. The sushi masterclass should also be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — depart by private car or JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station (approx. 1 hour). Visit the iconic Kotoku-in Great Buddha (Daibutsu) — a 13.35-meter bronze statue from 1252. Explore the Hase-dera Temple with its panoramic ocean views and cave of votive offerings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — Kamakura's most important Shinto shrine, approached via a grand avenue of cherry trees. Explore the surrounding Komachi-dori shopping street for premium Kamakura crafts, sweets, and lacquerware. Visit the Zen temples of Engaku-ji and Kencho-ji in Kita-Kamakura.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Farewell dinner at one of Tokyo's most celebrated restaurants — consider a reservation at Saito, Quintessence, or a comparable three-Michelin-star establishment for an unforgettable final dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a Kamakura restaurant specializing in shojin ryori (Zen Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) near the temples (¥5,000–¥10,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a three-Michelin-star Tokyo restaurant — the ultimate expression of Japanese culinary mastery (¥50,000–¥100,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is approximately 50km south of Tokyo. A private car allows flexible timing. The Great Buddha and Hase-dera are within easy walking distance of each other. Book the farewell dinner 2–3 months in advance — three-star reservations are extremely competitive.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit a favorite neighborhood or experience you wish to repeat. Consider a quiet early morning walk around the Imperial Palace moat (a 5km loop popular with locals), or a final visit to a neighborhood market. Pick up last-minute premium Japanese gifts at the hotel's recommended shops or a Chiyoda department store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and arrange private luxury transfer to the airport. Allow ample time for check-in, duty-free shopping, and departure formalities. Tokyo's major airports offer excellent duty-free selections of Japanese whisky, sake, cosmetics, and confectionery.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of culinary discovery, cultural immersion, and technological wonder in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor a last traditional Japanese breakfast of grilled fish, miso soup, pickles, and rice, or a Western set
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport — premium airport restaurant such as the ANA Lounge or a terminal sushi counter (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights from Narita (NRT) and 2.5 hours from Haneda (HND). Arrange private airport transfer the night before to confirm timing. Ensure all purchased items comply with customs regulations for your destination country.
